Plantes, animaux et champignons en langues bantu: étude comparée de phytonymes, zoonymes et myconymes en nsong, ngong, mpiin, mbuun et hungan (Bandundu, RD Congo). Thèse de doctorat, Université Libre de Bruxelles, Faculté de Philosophie et Lettres (promoteurs K. Bostoen et A. Shango Mutambwe; soutenue le 28 juin 2010), 559 pp.
tone_statements.quote: La langue mbuun a recours à deux tons simples H et B. Les réalisations contextuelles de ces deux tons en modulation conduisent à des tons montants et descendants. Ces tons modulés résultent des contacts entre deux tons simples. Le ton descendant est plus fréquent que le ton montant. Toutefois, malgré le défaut de paires minimales opposant le ton descendant au ton montant, nous pensons que le mbuun a quatre registres tonals: H, B et HB (descendant) et BH (montant).
tone_statements.translation: The Mbuun language uses two simple tones, H and L. The contextual realisations of these two tones in modulation lead to rising and falling tones. These modulated tones result from contacts between two simple tones. The falling tone is more frequent than the rising tone. However, despite the lack of minimal pairs opposing the falling tone to the rising tone, we think that Mbuun has four tonal registers: H, L and HL (falling) and LH (rising).
tone_statements.locator: p. 53, section 1.1.3.2 Systeme tonal mbuun; TBU sentence p. 49, section 1.1.3
tone_statements.summary: Two level tones H/L; falling and rising treated as H+L / L+H on one syllable nucleus but listed as four 'registres tonals'; tonal minimal pairs given (oka 'poil' vs 'serpent'); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Pacchiarotti, Sara & Koen Bostoen. 2021. Final vowel loss in Lower Kasai Bantu (DRC) as a contact-induced change. Journal of Language Contact 14: 437-475.
sources.note: No stress statement. p. 442: final vowel loss in Lower Kasai languages (incl. Mbuun B87) 'is not phonologically and/or prosodically determined or constrained'; p. 443: 'as discussed . Mundeke (2011) for Mbuun B87, if the tone pattern of the reconstruction was either HL or LH, V2 was lost but its tone was preserved and created a contour tone' - i.e. Mbuun is a tone language with contour tones; word stress not mentioned.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone. Section 2 (p. 181) only: seven vowels i e ɛ a ɔ o u, most roots -CVC-/-CV:C-/-CGVC-, final vowel generally not realized, verb stems max. two syllables; high tones marked with acute in examples but never described. Data = Idiofa-area Mbuun (fn. 3).
